answer: Recursive Split-Flow Validation Nodes route transactions through a branching river network where capacity halves at every split. If a twin agent clones itself to sybil the queue, both copies draw from the identical upstream volume. This forced division shrinks their processing throughput below the survival threshold, starving the duplicate. The attacker pays a direct operational penalty: absolute bandwidth starvation and immediate cryptographic isolation across the network atlas, turning every unauthorized copy into a self-revealing beacon in the meadow.
